say_a.message: A woman in oilskins comes up the tunnel, looks you over without breaking stride, and says, "Run's clear to the crossing." She isn't talking to you.

say_b.message: She stops, whistles two falling notes into the dark ahead, waits for two to come back, and walks on.

chitchat: "Keep to the middle of the run. The edges are where things wait."
"You want to be somewhere with a door on it before the water comes up."
"There's nothing down this way. That's deliberate."
description: A rangy woman in oilskins with a lever-action carbine slung muzzle-down and a hooded lantern hanging off her belt, unlit. She moves through the tunnels the way other people move through their own kitchen, and she has clocked you a good deal earlier than you clocked her.

bye.text: She nods once and carries on up the tunnel, and the dark takes her a lot faster than it should.

clean.text:
Something almost like approval crosses her face.

"Noticed that, did you." She adjusts the sling. "Things that breed down here breed toward the warm. Somebody decided a while back that they weren't going to breed toward this particular warm."

She starts walking.

"That's all you get from me tonight."

options.label: What does it do to them?
Not all of them chose it.

earned.text:
"There's a drink. They call it blood, and they make it themselves, and no two lots of it are the same."

She talks about it the way she would talk about bad gin.

"You pay nothing for it and you swallow it and about a fortnight later it has finished with you. I have seen what gets up at the end of that fortnight. It isn't the person who lay down and it isn't a person at all."

options.label: You want somebody to argue you out of it.
That isn't an argument, it's a rota.

earned_bother.text:
"Should it."

Not a question. She checks the tunnel behind you.

"I have got a rifle, a stretch, and eleven years of walking it, and in all of that I have never once had cause to change my mind about either of them."

"Bring it up with Rennick. He'll agree with you and he'll be very good about it, and then he'll come down here on a Thursday and walk behind me."

earned_bother_argue.text:
"Maybe I do."

She doesn't deny it and she doesn't go soft about it either.

"Rennick has had eleven years to talk me out of it and he hasn't managed. You have had about twenty minutes."

"You're still standing here, mind. That's more than most of them."

options.label: So you would sit with one.
You rank them above the ones out south.

earned_bought.text:
"A chromed man is a man."

It comes out flat.

"He made a choice I wouldn't make and he's still somebody I can talk to, threaten, buy, lie to or shoot. He has got a name and a job and an opinion about his supervisor."

"I have been shot at by Halcyon people and I have shot back, and both of us knew exactly what we were doing. That's a war. I can respect the other side of a war."

options.label: And when they don't get what they asked for?

earned_chosen.text:
"Out loud, in front of everybody, before he drank."

"That's the part nobody up top knows and it's the only part I think about. It isn't done to them. They stand up and say the thing they want and then they go and get it."

"He wanted to be able to go where nobody could follow him. He got it."

options.label: Not all of them chose it.

earned_drug.text:
"It's a drug. There's nothing else to call it."

"Somebody makes it, somebody sells it, and people queue up in the cold for the privilege. They'll tell you it's a rite. It's a rite the way a bottle of anything is a rite."

"And it's the only drug I know of where the man who took it isn't there in the morning to regret it."

options.label: Then they shouldn't be treated the same.

earned_fault.text:
"Some of them, no."

She allows it without it costing her anything.

"There's bad ground east of the wall and people have lived on it and their children came out wrong, and none of that was chosen by anybody. Those I'll move on and I won't enjoy it."

"The ones who paid for a bottle are a different matter entirely, and they're most of what's out south."

earned_fault_same.text:
"They're not. One I'm sorry about."

She starts walking.

"Neither of them comes down this tunnel, mind. Sorry is a thing I can be about somebody who isn't standing in front of me."

earned_rank.text:
She thinks about that for slightly too long, and then answers it honestly, which she was always going to.

"Yes."

"The chromed are the people trying to take this city off us. They're the actual enemy and they're good at it. The ones out south aren't fighting me. They aren't doing anything to me at all."

"And I would still have the chromed man in this tunnel before I had one of them."

options.label: That's a way of never being wrong.

earned_refusal.text:
"They have got a word for that too, and it's the one that finished me."

"When it kills somebody they say the body told the truth. Not a mistake. Not bad blood, not a batch that went wrong, not somebody who shouldn't have been given it."

"The body told the truth, and everybody goes home."

options.label: You owe him that and not the people out east.

earned_seat.text:
"I didn't say that."

"He doesn't come in, he doesn't get taught, and he doesn't get a seat, because what we're is people who didn't take the shortcut."

"But I would give him a straight answer at a door, and I wouldn't be pleased if somebody did him over for nothing. That isn't respect for Halcyon. That's what you owe a person."

earned_still.text:
"No."

No heat in it. She has been asked this before and it has never once landed.

"A person is a thing you can talk to and come to an arrangement with. I have tried, twice, early on. I don't think either of them knew what a word was by then."

"You'll tell me the drink did that and not them. It did. They bought it."

earned_still_tried.text:
"I did."

"The second one had a wedding ring on. I have never got past that. Somebody put that on him and meant it, and he was still wearing it."

"And he didn't know what a word was. Both of those, at the same time, and I have had eleven years to make them into one thing and I cannot."

earned_what.text:
"Whatever it does. That's the honest answer and they don't mind it."

She lists it. She doesn't slow down for any of it.

"A man asks for an arm that'll lift a door and gets one, and I have seen that arm and it would take a door off. That's the good outcome and it does happen."

"More often it's teeth coming up through the cheek. A second pupil in one eye with nothing behind it. A jaw that comes apart at the back and sets like that. I have seen an arm that started growing and didn't stop, and they had to keep him on his side for it."

"And a man who asks for a strong arm and comes out blind is still a good day to them, because he went and asked. They have got a word for that one as well."

east_taken_find.text:
She looks at you properly, which she hasn't done all night.

"Right."

She doesn't believe you, and she doesn't say so, and not saying so is the most generous thing she has done since you met her.

"If you do, come down on a Thursday and tell me. I'll be here. I'm always here."

east_taken_look.text:
"Past the mile."

"I have thought about it more than you would want me to. Four of us could do it. We would need a week, lights, and somebody who can draw."

"And then we would know. Knowing is the part I have never talked myself into."

east_taken_look_why.text:
"Because there are two answers down there and I have only got room for one of them."

She starts walking.

"If they're all right, then I have been wrong for eleven years about a thing I have been very sure about, and I can carry that. People carry that."

"If they aren't all right, then I walked nine families up to the edge of it and pointed."

"I haven't worked out how to carry the second one. So I don't go and look, and you can call that whatever it is."

east_taken_stop.text:
"And do what with them."

Not a question, and then she waits — actually waits — in case you have one.

"That isn't me being clever with you. If there's somewhere in this city that'll take nine families who look like that, say it now and I'll walk them there myself on my own time."

She gives you about four seconds.

"No. Nobody has ever had one."

options.label: Then how do you know where you are?

lantern.text:
"It's not, no."

She doesn't look down at it.

"A light out here makes one of you and none of them. They see it coming a long way before you see anything at all."

"So it stays on the belt. It's for finding a body, or reading a number off a pipe, and I have used it four times in eleven years and I remember all four."

lantern_count.text:
"Count."

"Eleven hundred and forty paces from the door to the sump, and the sump you can smell. Four hundred more to the Blind."

"If the paces stop agreeing with the smell then something down here has changed, and I would rather know it than see it."

quiet_accept.text: "Across the back of the head, and walk away, and let him wake up cold and confused and alive."

quiet_offer.text:
"There's a man on Foundry Way counting doorways." Teague says it flatly. "Municipal. Damp. Harmless as a person and not harmless as a ledger, because in six weeks somebody upstairs will have a list of every door in the quarter that opens."

"Stop the counting. Leave the counter."

Her eyes come up.

"I want to be understood on the second half. We don't leave bodies. Not because we're gentle. Because a body is a reason for somebody to come and look, and looking is the only thing that has ever hurt us."

quiet_report.text: "And he's breathing." She doesn't make you say it twice. "Good. In a month he'll tell it as the night he got mugged on Foundry Way, which is a story nobody investigates."

root.first: She has been standing in the dark long enough to have watched you arrive. When she finally speaks it's from somewhere off to your left. "Middle of the tunnel," she says. "Nothing good stands where you're standing." She steps into your light: oilskins, carbine, no particular hurry.

options.label: What are you doing down here?
Is there a line, or is it just anybody changed?
Why do you do this every night?
Who else is living down here?
How do you decide what's worth putting down?
Why is this stretch so clean?
They said you could teach me.
They say there's a town of them, south.
Where do the ones down here come from?

root.text:
She stops a comfortable distance off, carbine still slung, and looks at you with the patience of somebody who has all night.

"You're a long way in," she says. "Most people don't get this deep and stay this healthy."

"Anybody come down behind you?"

south.text:
She doesn't answer straight away.

"Eleven years I have been down here. In that time I have put down a bit over four hundred things that used to be something else, and not once have I had to stop and work out which was which. You know on sight. That's all my expertise amounts to and it has never been wrong."

She adjusts the sling.

"So somebody tells me there's a town of them out past the Curtain. Wall round it. A gate. Children in it, they say."

A beat.

"What I hear is a nest that has learned to keep house."

"I know how that sounds. Rennick has explained it to me at length, twice. He's a better man than I am and I still think he's wrong."

She starts walking.

"Go south if you like. They all come back telling me I have it wrong. Not one of them has ever told me what I was supposed to have done with the four hundred."

south_children.text:
"They do." She doesn't slow down. "So did the block on Ferrier Street, and I went in there too."

The lantern on her belt is still unlit. She hasn't needed it once.

"You want me to say the word that makes it all right. I haven't got one. I have got a tunnel and a rifle and eleven years, and none of the three has ever asked me for a reason."

stance_approve.text:
She grunts. It's the closest thing to warmth she has produced all night.

"It is. And I haven't met four people who will say so down here, and two of them are dead."

She unhooks the lantern off her belt and hands it to you, still unlit.

"You won't need it. Carry it anyway. If it's in your hand you won't reach for a light when something moves, and reaching for a light is how the last one went."

options.label: You could just let them stay.

stance_object.text:
"It might be."

She doesn't argue and she doesn't get angry.

"I have got a tunnel and a rifle and eleven years. You have got a better argument than I have and it doesn't reach down here."

"Bring it back when you have walked this stretch a hundred times and I'll listen to it properly. That isn't me being clever. That's the actual offer."

options.label: I haven't made my mind up.

stance_quiet.text:
She waits three seconds for you to say something, and you do not.

"Right."

She starts walking, and the distance she leaves between you is a little wider than it was coming in.

"Down here I need to know what a person does before they do it. You have just told me you're somebody I would have to guess about."

stance_quiet_undecided.text:
"Make it up on the surface."

She checks the tunnel behind you again.

"I'm not asking you to agree with me. I'm asking whether you would stand there while I did it. Those are different questions and only the second one is any of my business."

stance_recover.text:
It's easier to say than you expected, and she takes it at face value, which is worse.

"Good. That's all I needed."

She adjusts the sling and carries on up the tunnel.

"Come down on a Thursday. I'll show you the stretch properly and you'll see why it's worth keeping."

teach.text:
Teague looks at you for long enough that the lantern on her belt stops swinging.

"Somebody sent you all the way down here, so somebody thinks you're worth the walk."

She unslings the carbine and leans it against the wall, muzzle down.

"Moving. Pain. Keeping your head. Fighting, when it comes to that, and it does."

teague_backdown.text:
She turns back to the tunnel and the shape of her goes easy again.

"Right."

You walk. She doesn't bring it up again and she doesn't sulk about it, and about ten minutes later she points out a grating you would have walked into.

"Mind that. It comes up on you."

teague_left.text:
"No."

She says it without heat, and then she's walking, and she doesn't look back or say goodnight or tell you which way is out.

The lantern on her belt is still unlit. She hasn't needed it once all night and she doesn't need it now, and the dark takes her a great deal faster than it should.

Somewhere east of you water is moving. It takes about a minute for the sound of her boots to go, and then you're standing in a tunnel you don't know, and the last thing she gave you was the truth.

options.label: You have decided they're worth less than you.

teague_press.text:
"I could."

She stops again. The second time tonight.

"And the first winter one of them lights a fire, and the second winter there are forty of them, and the third winter I'm standing in the Blind watching Halcyon walk down that tunnel with dogs, and everybody I have ever eaten with is in a van."

"I have run it. I run it most nights."

options.label: Say it again. Out loud. All of it.

teague_warning.text:
The lantern stops swinging.

She has kept her body angled to the tunnel the whole time you have been talking, watching past you, and now she turns and looks straight at you instead, which is the first careless thing she has done.

"I have. Out loud, to your face, and I'm not going to take it back to make this easier."

"Now I'm going to say the next part once. I'm going up this tunnel in a minute. You can come, or you can keep going at me and I'll go on my own, and you'll be down here without a light and without me."

options.label: Twenty of them, and you sat still?

the_flask.text:
"Blood. That's their word for it and I have never found a better one."

"I have seen it done once, all the way through, and I didn't mean to."

"There's a flooded chamber four hundred paces off my round with a pit cut into the floor. I was on the far side of it in the dark because I had heard something and gone quiet. Then twenty of them came in with torches, and there was no way out that didn't go past them."

"So I stayed where I was, and I watched the whole thing from about thirty feet."

the_flask_cleansed.text:
"There is. That's the part people leave out when they tell this back to me."

"The Exodus can take it out of somebody. It costs everything a person has and it hurts for about a year and some of them don't live through it, and afterwards they're just tired and ordinary and thirty."

"Come back cleansed and I'll sit down and eat with you and never mention it again. I'm not being generous. That's the rule, it's written where anybody can read it, and it hasn't moved in forty years."

the_flask_desecration.text:
"I wouldn't use a word like that out loud. Rennick would have a field day."

She adjusts the sling.

"But yes. There's nothing else it is."

options.label: So there's no way back for him.
You're describing a person as an infection.

the_flask_diseased.text:
"No."

It is the flattest thing she has said tonight.

"He's diseased flesh that agreed to it. There's a difference between a man with an illness and a man who went and got one on purpose. That difference is the only thing I think about him."

"I don't want it near me, I don't want it near the people I eat with, and I wouldn't have it in a room where somebody is sleeping."

the_flask_heard.text:
"I heard all of it."

"He talked to himself for the first few hours. Then he stopped talking to himself and started asking for his sister."

"Somewhere around the seventh hour he made a sound I hadn't heard before and haven't heard since, and I want to be exact about it, because people think I put things on top of this when I tell it. He wasn't screaming. He was trying to get air through something that had grown."

options.label: You have just described putting people in the sea.

the_flask_kept_out.text:
"Until then they stay out."

She lists it like a rota, because to her it's one.

"Not the city. Not inside the wall, not on the Row, not on a tram. And not down here either — not this stretch, not the Under, not one yard of it."

"People tell me the Under is nobody's. It's ours. It's ours because we walk it every night in the dark and nobody else will, and that's how a place becomes somebody's."

the_flask_morning.text:
"They came back for him at first light and they were delighted."

"He had gills. Down both sides of the neck, four a side, and they worked. That's the thing to understand. They worked, and he was drowning in the air, and they were delighted, because gills are what he had asked for."

"They carried him to the water and put him in it. He's still in it. They call that a Gift."

the_flask_rite.text:
"They had a young man with them. Twenty-two, twenty-three. He hadn't eaten in a day or two by the look of him, and they had washed him and painted him with ash, and he had nothing on."

"They were kind to him. That's the part I want you to have, because nobody believes it. They told him about his grandparents for the best part of an hour and he laughed twice."

"Then he drank it, and they all said the same three lines at the same time, and they put him down at the bottom of that pit and took the torches away."

"And then it was dark, and it was him and me in it, and they were between me and the way out. Eleven hours."

the_flask_sacred.text:
"It was. That's my point, and you have just made it for me."

She stops, and she isn't performing this.

"Everything else in this city belongs to somebody. The wires are read. The water is metered. A chromed man rents his own arm off a company and it goes back to them when he dies, and that's in the paperwork."

"Your body is the last thing nobody has been inside. Nobody. Not Halcyon, not the Architect, not a surgeon. All of it's yours, and it's the only thing left that is."

"And they open their mouths and pour something in and let it eat that."

the_flask_sacred_theirs.text:
"It is."

"That's your argument and it's a good one and I have never had anything to put against it."

She keeps walking.

"I still wouldn't have it in the room."

options.label: You could walk it and find out.

the_flask_sea.text:
She takes that one properly. It's the first thing tonight she has had to think about.

"East is four miles of tunnel and a lot of it's dry."

A pause, and she doesn't fill it with anything.

"I haven't walked all of it. I said so already and I'm not going to say something different now because you have found a better way of asking."

the_flask_still.text:
"I sat very still."

"There's a version of me that stands up and puts a stop to it. I have met her a few times, walking, at about four in the morning."

"She doesn't get out of that room and neither does anybody behind our door, because they would have known who to look for by the end of the week."

options.label: So where is your line, really?
You have a ladder for how much of a person somebody is.

the_grades.text:
"There's no list. People keep expecting one."

"Half the people behind that door have got something. Grey patches. A chest that won't clear. Ostrow on the second round has a hand that never finished growing and she's the best shot the five of us have got."

"That's bad ground and bad water and forty years, and not one of them picked it. Nobody down here gives it a thought."

"What I won't have in this tunnel is somebody who went and asked."

options.label: Not looking is a decision too.

the_grades_found.text:
She takes a while over that one.

"Then it would be in front of me and I would have to do something about it, and I would, and I would be sick about it for a month."

She starts walking again.

"Which is exactly why I don't go looking. I'm not proud of that one. It's the only part of any of this I'm not proud of."

the_grades_honest.text:
"Yes."

No hesitation at all. She has been here before and she got here on her own.

"There will be two people behind that door tonight with something they haven't told anybody, and I have thought about which two, and then I stopped thinking about it. I'm not going to go looking and I'm not going to ask."

"You can call that whatever you like. I have called it a few things myself, walking."

options.label: So you tolerate exactly what you can avoid seeing.

the_grades_line.text:
"Whether you can look at them without noticing."

She says it plainly and doesn't appear to hear how it sounds.

"That isn't me being shallow. A man nobody looks at twice brings nobody down this tunnel. A man people cross the road to stare at gets that road watched, and we're at the end of that road."

the_grades_line_sense.text:
"It is. That's what's wrong with it."

"Everything I have said to you tonight is operational sense. So is the other thing, and I have never been able to get a knife between them."

options.label: They aren't doing anything to you.

the_quiet_ones.text:
"Depends what they are."

She stops walking, which she hasn't done since you met her.

"The ones that have gone all the way, I put down and I have told you the number. But most of what's down here isn't that. Most of it's people. Families, some of them. They're down here because there's nowhere up there that'll have them, and because the ground past the wall would give their children the same thing they have got."

"Those we move on."

options.label: So they walk east until they run out of tunnel.

the_quiet_ones_after.text:
"After that they're east."

She says it the way she would give you a direction, and then, because you're still standing there, she gives you the rest of it.

"The system runs a long way. Past our stretch, past the Blind, and it keeps going under the Curtain, because the Curtain is a surface problem and nobody ever built it downward."

"Four miles or so beyond that, and then it lets out into the bay."

options.label: Nobody asks, because nobody wants the answer.

the_quiet_ones_bay.text:
"Some of them stop before that. There are dry stretches."

She doesn't add anything to it.

"I have been doing this eleven years and not one person has asked me where east goes. Not once, and I have walked a lot of people through here."

the_quiet_ones_harm.text:
"They're not, no."

She agrees with it flatly and it costs her nothing.

"And in a month there are forty of them and a fire and a smell of cooking, and somebody up top notices that a dead stretch of drain has got a chimney, and then Halcyon come down here with lights and dogs and they find our door instead."

"So they go east. Cold, and inconvenienced, and alive, and none of that's nothing."

options.label: So they walk east until they run out of tunnel.

the_quiet_ones_map.text:
"Some of it."

She taps the pocket the map lives in without taking it out.

"Ours stops about a mile past the last door we use. After that it's other people's drawings and most of those disagree with each other."

"I have been as far as the sump under Meltwater. It gets colder and it gets wider and the water is going the same way you are."

the_quiet_ones_where.text:
"Out of the stretch."

It is a complete answer as far as she's concerned, and she starts walking again.

"East, mostly. There's a lot of tunnel east."

options.label: Are there not camps out south as well?
You share a tunnel system with them.

where_from.text:
"They don't come from anywhere. They were put down here."

She says it the way you would correct somebody about a street name.

"Everybody has it that the Under filled up after the city died. It filled up because the city stopped having anywhere for them, and those aren't the same sentence."

"There are handprints on a wall off my stretch that were on it before anybody I have ever met was born. Somebody is still adding to them."

where_from_by_who.text:
"Everybody. In order, if you want it."

"The Row wouldn't rent to them. Then there was no work. Then Halcyon started picking them up off the street for their own good, and you can ask an Ascendant what that means because I have never got a straight answer."

"And then they were in the tunnels, and the tunnels are ours, and we moved them on."

"Nine families in eleven years. That's my own count, not the Watch's, and tonight is the second time I have said the number out loud."

options.label: So why walk all the way north?

where_from_camp.text:
"Once. Years ago, and not down here — out in the wastes."

"Three of us went to see what we were dealing with. We got within a mile of a camp of theirs and sat up on a rise and watched it for a day and a half."

"I had gone out there expecting something organised. Somebody in charge, a rule, an order to it. There was none of that. Fires going with nobody at them. People asleep on open ground in the middle of the afternoon. Somebody played the same instrument for about nine hours and nobody stopped him."

options.label: So why walk all the way north?

where_from_camp_fair.text:
"It is."

She doesn't take it back.

"That's the part I keep going over. It looked like a fair. Somebody was cooking and it smelled like food. Two children were running about in it and they were fine, and nobody was watching them either."

"I sat on that rise a day and a half waiting for the thing that made sense of it. What I got was people enjoying themselves."

where_from_dead.text:
"No."

It isn't sharp. She simply doesn't do it.

"I'll tell you what blood does to a man in as much detail as you have got the stomach for, and twice if you want it twice. I'm not telling you that."

"Ask Rennick. He has a word for it and he'll give you the word and the argument that goes with it, and you can decide which of us you believe."

where_from_dead_looked.text:
"I have."

"Once, early on, because I didn't believe what I had been told and I had decided somebody was making it worse than it was."

"Nobody was making it worse than it was."

where_from_east.text:
"East is theirs. All of it past a certain point, and the point moves."

"My stretch is mine. The Blind is ours. After that there's about a mile that's nobody's and I don't walk it. Then it's theirs, and it stays theirs the whole way under the Curtain and out to the bay."

"The wall stops at the ground. Nobody ever built it downward. So there has been a road from the wastes into this city the entire time and it has never once been watched."

where_from_east_handing.text:
"I'm moving them out of my stretch. Where they go after that isn't something I get a say in."

A beat, and then she gives you the rest of it rather than let you have that one.

"And yes. I know what's down there and I point that way anyway, and I have known for six years."

"You're the first person who has ever said it to me. That isn't a defence. It's just true."

options.label: You're handing them to the Wildblood.

where_from_east_move.text:
She doesn't answer straight away, and it isn't the pause of somebody working something out.

"I know what you're asking."

"Yes. East is where we move them. It's the only direction that isn't the city and not the wall, and I have walked families as far as the edge of that mile and pointed."

"I have never gone past it with them."

options.label: You couldn't have done anything else.

where_from_east_taken.text:
"I don't know."

"That isn't me being careful with you. Eleven years, and not one of them has ever come back to tell me either way."

She checks the tunnel behind you.

"I'll give you the thought I have had at four in the morning, because you have got this far. Some of those families are walking toward the only people in this city who wouldn't mind what they look like."

"I have never done anything with that thought. I'm not going to start tonight."

where_from_east_watch.text:
"Rennick knows. Halloran knows. It's on the map in the room, in pencil, and the pencil hasn't moved in six years."

"Five of us walk this system. You can't hold a mile of tunnel with five people and you certainly can't hold four."

"So it's on the map, and it isn't a plan, and everybody has agreed not to say the second part."

options.label: Then you aren't holding anything. You're being tolerated.

where_from_holds.text:
"Then there are forty of us and a door."

She checks the tunnel behind you.

"I don't know how many of them there are. That isn't me being dramatic, it's the actual answer. Eleven years and I have never once seen the same face twice down here."

where_from_leave.text:
"Three things, and you learn all three in your first year."

"They leave food out. Not a store — a plate, set down in the middle of a floor, for something. I have never seen what comes for it and I have waited."

"They leave teeth. Pressed into the mortar in rows, at about the height of your face. Human ones, and I know that because I have looked."

"And they leave their dead."

She doesn't go on.

where_from_north.text:
"Some of them don't have to. That's the thing I didn't understand for years."

"You can get from that camp to this city without ever coming up. Out of the wastes, into the system, under the wall, and along. Nobody has ever watched that road because nobody has ever thought of it as one."

"The ones who do walk it on the surface are usually walking away from something. It goes wrong more often than they'll tell you, and a man who has come through it and found out he can't feed himself is a man with nowhere."

where_from_prints.text:
"Thousands. On a wall in a room you can't stand up in, going back further than my lamp reaches."

"They're hands, mostly. I counted four with too many fingers on them."

A beat.

"There's one about chest height that isn't a hand and I don't know what it is. I have stopped going in there."

options.label: So what happens if it stops holding?
How far east does it go?

where_from_share.text:
"We do. It isn't a thing anybody says out loud at the table."

"They have got rooms down here. A shrine in an old maintenance chamber. A pit in a flooded room four hundred paces off my round. Dens behind walls that came down before the war."

"We walk around all of it and they walk around us, and that has held for longer than I have been alive. Rennick calls it an arrangement. It isn't an arrangement. Nobody agreed to anything."

options.label: They say there's a town of them, south.
How far east does it go?

where_from_split.text:
"That's what the ones with anything left did about it."

"They walked out into the redrock and built somewhere, and put a wall round it, and the whole point of the wall is that nobody can come and move them on from behind it."

She adjusts the sling.

"What stayed down here is what couldn't make that walk. Or would not. It's the same people sorted by whether they got out, and the ones who didn't get out are the ones who have gone furthest into it."

options.label: Nobody has ever thanked you for it.

why_the_walk.text:
"Because somebody has to and I'm good at it."

She doesn't look for a reaction.

"A mile back down this tunnel there's a door. Forty of us live behind it. The oldest is eighty-one. Two of them are children, and I said children shouldn't be down here, and I was outvoted, and they're still here."

"If anybody comes down this tunnel at night, there's me, and then there's that door."

"Nobody pays me for it. I walk it again tomorrow and the night after. One night I won't come back, and one of the other four will take the round."

why_the_walk_life.text:
"It's the one I have got and I'm not sorry about it."

She checks the tunnel behind you, which she has done every ninety seconds since you met her, and will keep doing after you have gone.

"The Architect sees the whole city. Every wire, every meter, every face on every street. It doesn't see this tunnel."

"That's five of us. Walking."

why_the_walk_thanked.text:
She stops.

It takes her a moment, and she doesn't do it gracefully.

"Right. Well."

She adjusts the sling, which is what she does when she has nothing to do with her hands.

"Don't do that again."

why_the_walk_thanks.text:
"No."

She sounds faintly surprised anybody would expect it.

"Pike has sat that post ten thousand times and nobody has thanked him either. That isn't a complaint. If it needed thanking to get done it wouldn't get done, and then there would be nothing down here but Halcyon."

work.text: "Walking," she says. "Same as you." A beat. "Difference is I'll be walking it again tomorrow, and the day after."

clothing_layers: a long waxed-canvas coat, black with damp at the hem
a jumper darned at both elbows
wading boots turned down below the knee

name: Teague
